rv.q: No one’s going to rain on Sheridan Smith’s parade: this is the best female performance to be seen in the West End since Imelda Staunton’s triumphant Oliverwinning performance as Momma Rose in Gypsy on the same stage.

But the jewel at the heart of this production is Smith. Brilliantly costumed by Matthew Wright in the garish outfits of a woman who loves clothes (the fancier the better) and doesn't give a hoot that she hasn't a scrap of taste, she belts her way through triumph and disaster with such full-hearted charm that you can only surrender to it.

Daresay Fanny Brice had it too. It’s not quite a one-woman show: there’s a fine chorus, strong support from performers such as Marilyn Cutts as Fanny’s briskly loving mother and Joel Montague as Fanny’s lovelorn accompanist.

Sheridan Smith Funny Girl triumphantly reinvents Brice for a new generation of musical theatre lovers, conveying with skill and heart this entertainer's emotive blend of professional success and personal vulnerability.
It's a touching, open performance: a superb star turn in a show that questions what it is that makes a star.
Smith is still terrific. Songs that have been inextricable from Streisand for decades are transformed.
Though it never quite soars, it is comprehensively done and will give plenty of pleasure.
